name: ostomy-application
description: Dual-platform (mobile + web) patient-facing app for ostomy care tracking.

scripts.//build:deps: Every workspace whose consumers typecheck against its BUILT output must be listed here, in dependency order. `packages/ui` was missing and CI caught it: a clean checkout has no `packages/ui/dist`, so `apps/web`'s typecheck could not resolve `@ostomy/ui` — while every local run passed, because a stale dist from an earlier build was still on disk. Adding a package here is not optional bookkeeping; it is the difference between `pnpm verify` meaning something on a fresh clone and meaning nothing.
scripts.build:deps: pnpm --filter @ostomy/core build && pnpm --filter @ostomy/seed build && pnpm --filter @ostomy/ui build
scripts.verify:build-artifact: pnpm --filter @ostomy/api build && node -e "require('./apps/api/dist/prisma/prisma.service.js'); console.log('built CJS artifact loads: apps/api/dist/prisma/prisma.service.js')"
scripts.verify:core-require: pnpm --filter @ostomy/core build && node apps/api/scripts/require-core-smoke.cjs && echo "apps/api (CommonJS) required @ostomy/core (ESM) built output successfully - ADR-0010 proof"
scripts.verify: pnpm run check:env && pnpm run format && pnpm run build:deps && pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test && pnpm run verify:build-artifact && pnpm run verify:core-require && pnpm run verify:api-client

pnpm.//overrides: multer: three high-severity DoS advisories (GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-g5hg-p3ph-g8qg) affect multer <2.3.0, and 2.2.0 is what `@nestjs/platform-express` pins. There is nothing to bump to: @nestjs/platform-express@latest IS 12.0.1, the version this repo already uses, and it still depends on multer@2.2.0 — so the override is the only route to a patched version until NestJS releases one. Remove it then, and not before. Safe here specifically because `apps/api` performs no multipart handling at all: there is no FileInterceptor, no @UploadedFile, and no multer import anywhere in src/, and none is planned — SRS_v2 section 4 routes photo uploads through S3 presigned URLs, so bytes never transit the API. multer is dead weight in the dependency graph that `@nestjs/platform-express` drags in regardless. This is scoped to a version range rather than pinned exactly so a 2.3.x patch is picked up without another commit.
pnpm.//overrides-react: One React for the whole repo, because `.npmrc` sets node-linker=hoisted. Hoisting puts a single react-dom at the root while a workspace whose range excludes the hoisted react keeps its own nested copy - so components render against one React instance and react-dom's dispatcher is bound to another. That does not error: it renders NOTHING, and packages/ui's suite failed 21 tests with an empty <div /> and no clue why. 19.2.3 is Expo SDK 57's pin and the version React Native 0.86 is tested against, so the native side chooses it and everything else follows. Raise this only in step with an Expo upgrade.
pnpm.//overrides-brace-expansion: brace-expansion: two high-severity DoS advisories (GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p and its follow-up) affect <1.1.20 on the v1 line and >=4.0.0 <5.0.11 on the v5 line. Both lines are present because the graph reaches brace-expansion through minimatch twice: eslint-config-prettier>eslint>minimatch pulls v1, expo>@expo/cli>glob>minimatch pulls v5. Neither is a dependency this repo chose or imports — both are build tooling — and the vulnerable path is parsing an attacker-supplied glob, which nothing here does: every glob in this repo is a literal in a config file. Two entries rather than one because no single range spans both majors and minimatch v3 requires brace-expansion ^1.1.7. Scoped to ranges rather than pinned, so a later patch is picked up without another commit. Remove each when its upstream ships a patched minimatch, and not before.
pnpm.//overrides-october-advisories: proxy-addr / shell-quote / source-map-js: three advisories that appeared together in October. All three are OVERRIDES rather than `ignoreCves` entries, and the distinction is the one the auditConfig note below records: each has a published patched version, so an override pins a real fix and then self-clears when upstream catches up — whereas an ignore suppresses by CVE id forever. Prefer an override whenever a patch exists. (1) proxy-addr <2.0.8, CRITICAL, IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped addresses. This is the one that is genuinely ours: it arrives as apps__api>@nestjs/platform-express>express>proxy-addr, i.e. inside the running API, and it is the code that decides which address a request came from. Everything the API does with a client address — the rate limiter keyed on the patient, the security log — reads what this package resolves, so a spoofable resolver is a real control being wrong rather than a dependency being noisy. (2) shell-quote >=1.8.4 <1.11.0, CRITICAL, command injection through `quote()`. Arrives as apps__mobile>react-native>react-devtools-core>shell-quote: React Native's devtools launcher, which is build-time tooling and is not in the shipped Android app. Pinned anyway because a patch exists and costs nothing. (3) source-map-js <1.2.2, high, event-loop denial of service through indexed source-map section offsets. Arrives as apps__mobile>expo>@expo/metro-config>postcss>source-map-js — the bundler's CSS pipeline, build-time only. Same reasoning as (2). Each is scoped to a version range rather than pinned exactly, so a later patch is picked up without another commit, and each becomes inert once the upstream dependency moves past it.
pnpm.//auditConfig: Two advisories are ignored rather than fixed, and the shared reason is that **there is no fix to apply**: both cover every published version of their package (`Patched versions: <0.0.0`), so an `overrides` entry like the brace-expansion ones above has no target. Both reach this repo only through expo>@expo/cli — build tooling, not code the Android app runs. `pr.yml`'s own comment states the policy this implements: "a build-tooling advisory with no available fix must not halt all work". (1) node-forge: GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv / CVE-2026-85393, high — RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements. The advisory covers <=1.4.0 and 1.4.0 is the latest published version. Nothing here verifies an RSA signature with it. (2) braces: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm / CVE-2026-93687, high, published 2026-09-18 — stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns. The advisory covers <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the latest published version (verified with `npm view braces versions`), and the GitHub advisory reports `first_patched_version: null`. It arrives as expo>@expo/cli>@expo/metro-file-map>micromatch>braces — Metro's file crawler, which runs at bundle time; `braces` is not in the shipped app. micromatch cannot be overridden past it either, since micromatch 4.x depends on braces ^3.0.3. Reaching the bug needs an attacker-supplied glob, and nothing here parses one: every glob in this repo is a literal in a config file — the same argument the brace-expansion overrides rest on. Three things to know about this mechanism. It is pnpm's declarative ignore list rather than a CI flag because `pnpm audit --ignore` and `--ignore-unfixable` both WRITE this very block into package.json when they run, so a flag in `pr.yml` would dirty the tree mid-job and silently suppress the advisory in the informational step that runs after it. Unlike an `overrides` entry it does NOT self-clear: the informational audit reports only a count of ignored advisories without naming them, so this comment is the only record of which. And an ignore is unconditional — if one of these packages later publishes a DIFFERENT advisory with the same CVE it stays suppressed, which is why each entry names a specific CVE rather than a package. Remove each the moment its upstream publishes a patched version; nothing else will tell you (#105).
